title: Homogeneous annihilator outside a homogeneous prime
statement: Let $S$ be an $\mathbb N$-graded commutative ring with grading $\mathcal A$, and $M$ an $S$-module internally graded by $\mathbb Z$ with grading $\mathcal M$, compatible with graded scalar multiplication. Let $x\in\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ correspond to a homogeneous prime $\mathfrak p$ [def-nagata-affine-proj]. If $y\in M_z$ and $c\notin\mathfrak p$ satisfy $cy=0$, there exist $k\in\mathbb N$ and $b\in S_k$ with $b\notin\mathfrak p$ and $by=0$.

proof.text: Decompose the scalar into homogeneous components. Internal direct-sum grading separates the components of c*y, so each component kills y; homogeneity of the prime gives one component outside it.

lean.statement:
theorem homogeneousVectorAnnihilator
    (𝓜 : ℤ → AddSubgroup M) (h𝓜 : DirectSum.IsInternal 𝓜)
    (hsmul : ∀ (n : ℕ) (z : ℤ) (a : S) (y : M),
      a ∈ 𝒜 n → y ∈ 𝓜 z → a • y ∈ 𝓜 (n + z))
    (x : Proj 𝒜) (z : ℤ) (y : M) (hy : y ∈ 𝓜 z)
    (c : S) (hc : c ∉ x.asHomogeneousIdeal) (hcy : c • y = 0) :
    ∃ (k : ℕ) (b : S), b ∈ 𝒜 k ∧ b ∉ x.asHomogeneousIdeal ∧ b • y = 0
